events.title: The financial crisis intensifies
events.description: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy. Authorities support other financial firms as stress spreads.

events.title: Deepwater Horizon disaster
events.description: An offshore drilling explosion kills workers and leads to a major oil spill.

events.title: Japan is struck by an earthquake and tsunami
events.description: Coastal communities suffer devastating damage and begin a long recovery.

what_happened_next.text:
Disney led the set, but the two homebuilders split sharply: Lennar gained while KB Home lost nearly three-fifths. Bonds gained more than the US basket. Housing trouble was already visible at the start, yet it still did not tell you which companies would recover or how long that would take.

Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy the following September as the financial crisis grew worse. The period also included the Deepwater Horizon disaster and Japan’s earthquake and tsunami. The chart covers years in which people faced several very different kinds of uncertainty.

The two homebuilders offer a concrete test of an industry story. Someone might have expected housing to recover, yet Lennar and KB Home did not give the same five-year result. Owning both would still have placed a lot of money in one kind of business. A broad basket spreads that reliance more widely, though it can also fall. The useful question is how much your plan depends on one forecast being right.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: The housing slowdown was spreading into finance. Branding, education and television also competed for attention.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: Companies in the same industry had different results. Owning two homebuilders was not the same as spreading money across many unrelated businesses.
reflection.what_faded_away: A builder’s sales incentive did not reveal its five-year stock return. A popular entertainment brand did not provide a precise forecast either.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The depth of the financial crisis and the eventual company rankings were unknown. Knowing there was trouble was different from knowing its outcome.

hot_stock_outcomes.text: The housing crash hurt Lennar badly: it lost about $1.1 billion in 2008 as home sales weakened and land values fell. By the quarter ended May 2012, new orders were up 40% from a year earlier and its homebuilding business was earning more money. That recovery helped the shares finish higher, despite a very difficult journey through the housing slump.

The housing crash cut deeply into KB Home’s business. Its annual revenue more than halved in 2008, and it lost about $976 million as sales shrank and it reduced the value of land and other assets. Conditions later improved, but the quarter ended May 2012 still brought a $24 million loss. The recovery had not repaired the damage to profits or the share price.

Disney added Marvel in 2009, bringing superheroes into its movies and merchandise. The Avengers became a major hit in May 2012. TV networks and parks also helped earnings grow, even while the costly film John Carter hurt movie profits earlier that year. Disney’s range of businesses helped it recover from the recession and finish these five years with a share-price gain.
